title: Meduza and Haaretz Both Reported Sanchez's Disinformation Charge — Without Rebuttal
subtitle: The outlets from the accused countries reported the accusation. The state outlets from the same countries reported something else entirely.
body_md:
In late August, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said on Cadena Ser radio that Russia and Israel had amplified disinformation to inflame the Ceuta migration crisis, which by then had killed at least 141 people and left roughly 5,000 migrants, including 1,200 minors, on the streets of the enclave. Sánchez called it "evident" that both countries had used the crisis to criticize his government, amid ongoing disagreements with Madrid over Ukraine and Gaza.

The global press ran the disinformation accusation as the lead story. One hundred forty-one deaths and 70,000 border crossings became context for a geopolitical blame narrative. [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/31/morocco-ceuta-border-breach-spanish-pm-migration-pedro-sanchez) reported Sánchez said "fake news had been pumped out on social media accounts." [Daily Sabah](https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/russia-israeli-disinformation-helped-trigger-ceuta-crises-spain-pm) headlined it: "Russia, Israeli disinformation helped trigger Ceuta crises: Spain PM." [France 24 Spanish](https://www.france24.com/es/video/20260831-qu%C3%A9-papel-atribuye-pedro-s%C3%A1nchez-a-israel-y-rusia-en-la-crisis-migratoria-de-ceuta) cited EU investigations as the institutional source for the claims, lending authority Sánchez himself did not explicitly invoke.

The Spanish domestic press ran a different story. [ABC.es](https://www.abc.es/espana/entrevista-pedro-sanchez-hoy-directo-declaraciones-ultimas-20260831081306-di.html) noted that Sánchez "denied CNI intelligence reports alerting to the severity of the crossing" — a domestic accountability question absent from all international coverage. [El Mundo](https://www.elmundo.es/espana/2026/09/01/6a96a8f7e4d4d821098b4587.html) framed the crisis through a constitutional lens: the Moncloa-Zarzuela distance, and King Felipe VI's 20-year absence from Ceuta now politically weaponized. [El Pais English](https://english.elpais.com/spain/2026-08-31/ceuta-the-month-that-broke-a-city.html) reported what the ground in Ceuta looked like: "hostility toward migrants is increasing among local residents who are fed up and feel abandoned by the central government. In a city that prides itself on religious coexistence, conflicts have already flared up between its Muslim and Christian communities."

The harshest international register came from [Daily Mail](https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-16095323/Thousands-migrants-streets-Rapes-violence-daily-occurrence-officials-warn-Ceuta-verge-disaster-worst-worst-enclave.html?ns_mchannel=rss&ito=1490&ns_campaign=1490): "Rapes and violence a daily occurrence. Now officials warn Ceuta is on the verge of disaster with 'the worst of the worst' still in the enclave." No other outlet in the corpus operated in that severity register. [RT Africa](https://www.rt.com/africa/644329-morocco-arrests-hundreds-migrants-attempted-crossing-ceuta/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=RSS), the sole Russian state outlet, took a different approach entirely: it reported Morocco's enforcement arrests of 294 migrants and 61 alleged facilitators, never mentioning Sánchez's disinformation accusations against Russia.

The corpus's most consequential finding is the behavior of the two outlets from the accused countries' opposition press. [Meduza](https://meduza.io/en/news/2026/08/31/spain-s-prime-minister-blames-networks-linked-to-russia-and-israel-for-spreading-fake-news-about-ceuta-migration-crisis) — the Russian exile outlet explicitly operating in opposition to the Kremlin — reported straight: "The investigation into what caused the migration crisis in Ceuta is still underway, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said on Cadena Ser radio, but social media has already been flooded with fake news and disinformation." [Haaretz](https://www.haaretz.com/world-news/europe/2026-08-31/ty-article/spains-sanchez-israel-amplified-disinformation-over-ceuta-migrant-crisis/000001a0-56f1-d822-a3b8-56ffe0370000) reported the same, noting Sánchez said it was "evident" that both countries had used the crisis against Madrid.

Neither outlet contested the accusation. Neither mounted an editorial defense of its government's conduct. This is noteworthy: RT Africa, the state outlet, ignored the story; Meduza, the anti-Kremlin outlet, reported it without challenge. Israel's foreign minister was quoted denying the accusations in other outlets, but Haaretz — Israel's leading left-liberal paper — published the accusation as reported fact. The two outlets most capable of providing internal rebuttal from within Russia and Israel instead effectively validated the frame from within.

What the corpus left unreported is the humanitarian accounting. Sánchez's geopolitical accusation dominated coverage of an event that killed 141 people crossing from Morocco. [Deutsche Welle](https://www.dw.com/en/protesters-set-fire-to-migrant-camp-in-ceuta/a-78538847?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf) reported that protesters had set fire to a migrant camp. [Sky News UK](https://news.sky.com/story/italy-and-spain-extend-tit-for-tat-border-controls-after-ceuta-migrant-surge-13579414) reported Italy and Spain extending tit-for-tat border controls — the EU policy response. Both were secondary notes in a corpus organized around who spread what on social media.
